rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi distinguishes God's eternal speech, an attribute of the speaker, from recited letters on created sound, which image it; mutawatir usage establishes the latter as God's speech by religious convention, figurative only as an image.
rows.anchor: بل هو صورة من صور كلامه القديم القائم به تعالى ومظهر تنزلاته فهو دال على الحقيقي القائم فسمى كلاما حقيقة شرعية لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says this reading is what al-Taftazani indicates, avoids the feared consequences, and shows that al-Mawaqif's objection rests on an assumption.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا يشير كلام التفتازاني فلا يلزم شيء من المفاسد وإعتراض صاحب المواقف مبني على ظنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his fifth reply, Al-Alusi says al-Mawaqif's pronoun may refer to the uttered content rather than the act of utterance; inner speech lacks sequence mentally, while external utterance orders it.
rows.anchor: أن كلام صاحب المواقف ليس نصافي أن الضمير راجع إلى التلفظ بل يحتمل أن يكون راجعا إلى الملفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus, the statement that it is created can refer to the externally uttered image, so proofs of createdness concern that image rather than inward speech and the objection falls away.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي هو حادث أي الملفوظ بالتلفظ الخارجي الذي هو الصورة حادث لا اللفظ النفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miracle objection assumes verbal Quran cannot be eternal divine speech; Al-Alusi answers that its descent into genuine Arabic wording is miraculous, while the eternal Quran is inner wording joined to meaning.
rows.anchor: المعجزة هو القرآن في مرتبة تنزله إلى الألفاظ الحقيقة العربية فكونه لفظا حقيقيا عربيا مجعول بالنص

rows.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
rows.claim: Al-Iji analyzes a statement into its wording, intended sense, the speaker's knowledge of the relation, and the relation's actual truth; the last two are not speech by consensus, and Ashʿarīs exclude the wording, leaving its meaning.
rows.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

rows.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
rows.claim: For command and prohibition, Iji likewise counts will or aversion, spoken wording, and its meaning; excluding the first and second under the Ashʿarī account leaves the concept as their inner speech.
rows.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

rows.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
rows.claim: Iji argues that defining inner speech as a meaning without letters conflicts with ordinary language and Arabic usage, where speech consists only of a combination of letters.
rows.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

rows.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
rows.claim: Iji argues that scripture repeatedly says God calls His servants and authentic reports specify a voice; treating over 100,000 explicit texts as metaphor is unreasonable.
rows.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

rows.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
rows.claim: Iji argues that one inner meaning cannot cover distinct commands, prohibitions, reports, and individual utterances; otherwise all scriptures would contain identical content, and speech would be both truth-apt and not truth-apt.
rows.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

rows.speaker: المعترض
rows.claim: A fifth objection says abrogation evidence concerns the uttered content, not the act of utterance, since some rulings are abrogated while their recitation remains.
rows.anchor: فلأن الأدلة الدالة على النسخ لا يمكن حملها على التلفظ بل ترجع إلى الملفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi distinguishes God's speech as the attribute of speaking from speech as what is spoken: the first is one attribute with relations to the many books and words, and is neither actual nor mental letters.
rows.anchor: الحق عز أسمه له كلام بمعنى التكلم وكلام بمعنى المتكلم به وما هو أمر واحد المعنى الأول وهو صفة واحدة تتعدد تعلقاتها بحسب تعدد المتكلم به

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam's cited proof says eternal speech has always been command, prohibition, and report; these classify what is spoken, so the unitary attribute with multiple relations is the first sense of speech.
rows.anchor: نقل الإمام أن الكلام الأزلي لم يزل متصفا بكونه أمرا نهيا خبرا ولا شك أن هذه أقسام المتكلم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi answers that the sequence objection applies only to actual external wording; mental wording has all its parts together in mental existence while retaining order, so al-Mawaqif can be read consistently.
rows.anchor: إذا أريد من اللفظ الحقيقي وأما إذا أريد النفسي الحكمي فلا ورود له لأن الألفاظ النفسية كلها مجتمعة الأجزاء في الوجود العلمي مع كونها مترتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the third objection assumes that real wording means external speech, but the term may mean inward wording, as the comparison with what exists in a memorizer suggests.
rows.anchor: الإيراد مبني على ظن أن المراد باللفظ الحقيقي مع أنه محتمل لأن يراد النفسي كما يقتضيه ظاهر تشبيهه بالقائم بنفس الحافظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi defines inner speech among the people of truth as the combination of inner wording and meaning, rather than meaning alone.
rows.anchor: الكلام النفسي عند أهل الحق هو مجموع اللفظ النفسي والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi explains that al-Mawaqif seems to have understood some Ashʿarīs as making inner speech pure meaning without wording, since they call verbal Quran God's speech only metaphorically.
rows.anchor: ظاهر كلام صاحب المواقف يدل على أنه فهم من ظاهر كلام بعض الأصحاب أن مرادهم بالمعنى هو المقابل للفظ مجردا عن اللفظ مطلقا
